intent: Pixel Pod design development using reference images
status: Concept only; not verified mechanical CAD
common_prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Industrial design concept development of the user's selected PIXEL POD handheld. Image 1 is the aesthetic reference: preserve its forest-green, warm cream and golden-yellow palette, friendly retro rounded-rectangle silhouette, small upper-center landscape screen, nine controls and upper-right RGB. It is NOT accurate mechanical CAD. Image 2 is the exact power PCB layout reference; do not rearrange its components. Create a fresh polished product concept sheet, white studio background, clear large assembled hero and one exploded assembly view with a few large clean labels. Smooth satin bed-contact cosmetic surfaces, not prominent layer ridges. These are finish goals, not claims of verified print quality. Main PCB 96x105 mm, power PCB 50x50 mm. Shell must contain the full main rectangle plus sockets and solder tails; substantial depth, not a thin phone or tiny keyfob. Small 280x240 landscape LCD active width roughly one third of body width, cheerful color pixel pet. Below display exactly FOUR separate direction buttons diamond left, FOUR action buttons diamond right (X upper, Y left, A right, B lower), ONE central mode button slightly lower. Single RGB optical lens near screen upper-right in protective raised pod. Exactly TWO IR apertures on TOP EDGE near left, not four and not in front face. No rear-facing power switch copied from old art.
POWER GEOMETRY: orient the entire referenced power board 180 degrees in its own plane and place its component face toward the removable back. In a straight REAR VIEW the power board is in the lower LEFT chamber: its USB now faces the bottom edge and its existing side-actuated switch faces the LEFT edge near bottom. Thus the external switch is on the user's RIGHT side in a FRONT view. One bottom USB-C near that power board, not centered arbitrarily. USB and switch on ADJACENT faces aligned with the SAME physical PCB, not opposite faces, no remote switch/no extra USB. Show this clearly in a small rear cutaway inset if needed.
INTERNALS: a structural insulated chassis with separate serviceable click-in carriers: main board + its screen as one supported assembly, power board on its own supported cradle, and battery in a separate smooth removable carrier in rear lower-right as seen from back. The BATTERY CARRIER clicks into the chassis; NEVER draw clips pressing the soft battery pouch. Battery shown as an unbranded blank placeholder with clearance, labeled BATTERY SIZE TBD. Release tabs reachable after opening; retain boards only at verified future safe supports, don't flex PCBs or load components. Keep top-center rear zone clear of battery, power board, wires, screws and metal for the ESP32 antenna. Indicate that zone as AIR / ANTENNA CLEARANCE, not fill it with cells. Internal assemblies schematic envelopes, not invented detailed circuitry. Wire channels and service clearance, no exposed battery against solder pins. Back removable, small captive screws can secure the outer cover while carriers click in.
Keep the same nine buttons in all assembled views. Show cosmetic panels parted from hidden chassis to explain how separate pieces can lie exterior-face-down on a print bed. NO dimensioned blueprint, STL claim, manufacturing certification, ears, extra controls, extra optics, photoreal electronics fabrication. Short title and footer CONCEPT ONLY - FIT AND PRINT TESTS REQUIRED. Clean attractive hierarchy, do not cram tiny paragraphs.

variants.title: A - FLAT PANEL PIXEL POD
variants.prompt: Recommended smooth-surface architecture. Preserve friendly Pixel Pod identity but use softened clipped/faceted corners, not continuous convex wraparound sides. Outer cosmetic shell consists of one flat cream front with separate flat green surround accents, one flat green back, four separate broad flat edge panels and small planar corner facets. Every major visible face can print face-down separately; edges and joints remain visible as neat intentional seams. A hidden structural chassis carries all loads. Use yellow accent inlays and button caps. Show exploded shell with front, rear, side panels and corner facets separated around the internal frame, plus small schematic three-carrier rear view. Add one small print-bed inset with two side skins lying broad EXTERIOR face DOWN, interior tabs UP. Title A - FLAT PANEL PIXEL POD. Label major groups only: FACE-DOWN SKINS, HIDDEN FRAME, CLICK-IN CARRIERS. Show subtle seams rather than claiming seamless molding. No large unbroken rounded 3D bumper whose external surface cannot touch a flat bed.

variants.title: B - SNAP SKIN PIXEL POD
variants.prompt: Keep the original Pixel Pod's rounder softer corners. Separate broad flat front and back plates plus two flat clip-on SIDE SKINS, separate flat top/bottom port strips, and four small rounded corner caps attached to a hidden frame. All large flat touch surfaces have a fine uniform bed-contact satin finish. The small curved corner caps are the remaining post-processing pieces: clearly label CORNERS: LIGHT SANDING / FINISH. Show skins sliding/clipping onto structural ribs with release tabs inside; do not make tiny fragile snap hooks. This offers fewer/more manageable decorative pieces than faceting every corner but does NOT pretend curved caps can be layer-free as printed. Hero view keeps original retro look, exploded shows skins detached and small rear inset locates actual power board, side switch, USB, separate battery carrier and antenna zone. Title B - SNAP SKIN PIXEL POD. Labels FACE-DOWN PANELS, REMOVABLE CORNER CAPS, CLICK-IN CARRIERS. Minimal clear art, no ridges on the finished hero, note finish required on curved caps.

variants.title: C - FINISHED PIXEL POD
variants.prompt: Alternative for truly visually line-free rounded exterior: fewer larger cosmetic pieces, a removable front face plate, rounded rear shell and separate button/accent pieces over the same click-in carrier chassis. Render the exterior as a FINISHED sanded, primed, painted satin target, not an as-printed miracle. Preserve exactly the original rounded friendly silhouette, color blocks and controls. Main hero smooth paint. Exploded view shows separate outer pieces and internal supported main/screen carrier, power cradle and non-compressing battery carrier. Small finish-process inset showing only disconnected empty plastic shell samples, never coating/sanding assembled electronics. Label PRINT > SAND > PRIME > PAINT. Title C - FINISHED PIXEL POD. State FINISHING REQUIRED. The goal is few exterior seams with more manual finishing; not vapor smoothing, no hazardous solvent instructions. Power switch and bottom USB still aligned with rotated actual power board; do not copy old rear switch.
